sources.title: Premtim Alaj, Iron Age settlements in Kosovo
sources.note: Doctoral archaeological synthesis of settlements, houses, objects, food work, crafts, imports, and cemeteries.

sources.title: Edi Shukriu, The Dardanian Kingdom
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis of settlement, fortification, burial, exchange, political identity, and chronology.

sources.title: Palaeohispanica, Palaeo-European languages in the Balkans
sources.note: Peer-reviewed treatment of limited Dardanian linguistic evidence and uncertain classification.

sources.title: The Romans and us: Strabo and the construction of ethnicity
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of Strabo as an author constructing ethnic categories rather than neutrally recording them.

sources.title: Livy, History of Rome, Book 31, chapter 28
sources.note: Primary Roman narrative naming Bato son of Longarus among leaders at the Roman camp in 200 BCE.

sources.title: Livy, History of Rome, Book 40, chapter 57
sources.note: Primary Roman narrative of Philip V and the Bastarnae plan directed against the Dardanians.

sources.title: Livy, History of Rome, Book 41
sources.note: Primary Roman narrative of the Bastarnae invasion, Dardanian resistance, winter fighting, and withdrawal.

sources.title: Livy, History of Rome, Book 43, chapter 18
sources.note: Primary Roman narrative for conflict and diplomacy involving Perseus and the Dardanians during the Third Macedonian War.

sources.title: Polybius, Histories, Book 28
sources.note: Primary Greek narrative context for Perseus, Rome, and Balkan diplomacy in the 170s BCE.

sources.title: Vladimir Petrovic, Pre-Roman and Roman Dardania
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of geography, communications, mining, Macedonian relations, and later Roman encounters.

sources.title: Erich Gruen, Hegemony to Empire: Macedonia Provincia
sources.note: University of California Press analysis of the 148 BCE provincial settlement and its historical limits.

sources.title: Naser Ferri, The Resistance of the Dardanians to Roman Conquests and Romanisation
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis of changing Dardanian relations with Rome after Macedonian conquest and later campaigns.

sources.title: Edi Shukriu, History of Ancient Dardania
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis of Dardanian political history, economy, agriculture, animal husbandry, crafts, and evidence limits.

sources.title: Premtim Alaj and Edi Baraliu, Iron Age settlements in Kosovo
sources.note: University archaeological study of hill, terrace, and lowland settlements, defenses, and domestic evidence.

sources.title: Archaeological Guide of Kosovo
sources.note: Official heritage guide to settlement forms, fortification, cemeteries, and archaeological sites.

sources.title: University of Pristina, Dardania in the Iron Age
sources.note: University teaching synthesis of Iron Age Dardania, material culture, settlement, and burial evidence.

sources.title: Kosovo Ministry of Culture, Cernica archaeological excavation
sources.note: Official report identifying a major Iron Age and Hellenistic settlement associated with the Dardanian kingdom.

sources.title: The funerary monument from Kulina
sources.note: Scholarly study of a distinctive funerary relief with human figures and military imagery.

sources.title: Review of the Romaja necropolis excavation
sources.note: Scholarly review of tumular burial evidence and its chronology at Romaja.

sources.title: Dollc tumuli and prehistoric cremation burial
sources.note: Report on an Institute of Archaeology monograph, cremation graves, human remains, and chronological limits.

sources.title: Mining, silver and coinage in ancient Macedonia and Dardania
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of ore districts, silver movement, and regional metal economies.

sources.title: Silver provenance and circulation in the central Balkans
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeometric study of silver, coins, vessels, imports, and exchange in the central Balkans.

sources.title: European Association of Archaeologists 2024 abstract book
sources.note: Research abstract on large storage jars, production, exchange, and routes between Dardania and Adriatic markets.

sources.title: British Museum, bronze figure of a running girl
sources.note: Museum catalogue record for an imported Archaic Greek bronze reportedly found near Prizren.

sources.title: Strabo, Geography, Book 7
sources.note: Ancient outsider description locating the Dardanians and supplying ethnographic claims that require caution.

sources.title: Pliny the Elder, Natural History, Book 4
sources.note: Ancient Roman geographic ordering of Balkan peoples, written later than the card interval.

sources.title: The Pervading Empire, preview chapter on Dardanian ethnography
sources.note: Modern scholarly interpretation of Strabo and Aelian stereotypes about housing, dung, music, and bathing.

sources.title: Serbian Encyclopedia, Dardanians
sources.note: Academic encyclopedia entry on names, language evidence, absence of a native script, and Greek or Latin use.

sources.title: Names and onomastics in Roman Dardania
sources.note: Scholarly study of later Roman-period personal names and inscriptions, useful as a chronological comparison.

sources.title: Roman inscriptions from Dresnik in Dardania
sources.note: Peer-reviewed publication of later Roman epigraphy, explicitly outside the card interval.

sources.title: Tooth wear in a Roman-era Dardanian sample
sources.note: Osteological study of 21 skulls and 498 teeth from the second to fourth centuries CE.

sources.title: Dea Dardanica and identity in Roman Dardania
sources.note: Scholarly critique of projecting a Roman-period cult backward as unchanged Iron Age ethnic religion.

sources.title: Archaeology, heritage, and statebuilding in Kosovo
sources.note: Research report on modern uses of Dardanian archaeology and disputed direct-descent narratives.

sources.title: Archaeology Magazine, Kosovo archaeology
sources.note: Archaeological overview of research, sites, preservation, and contested interpretation in central Kosovo.
